paragraphs: Birkat shehecheyanu beqiddush hallayla tzarik lebarek bishte hallelot, upoh irenu bagdad nohagim hannashim lebarek shehecheyanu behadlaqat hannerot bekol yom tob sheyyesh bo birkat shehecheyanu beqiddush:

clarification.explanation: At the Kiddush of Shavuot outside the Land of Israel, one recites the berachah of Shehecheyanu on both nights (of the first and second days of Yom Tov). In Baghdad the women were accustomed to recite Shehecheyanu at the time of lighting the candles, on every Yom Tov on which Shehecheyanu is also recited at Kiddush.
takeaways: Shehecheyanu is recited at Kiddush on both nights of Shavuot outside the Land of Israel
The Baghdad custom of women reciting Shehecheyanu when lighting candles

paragraphs: Haqqadosh ballayla harishona tzarik lihyot achar tzet hakkokabim diktib sheba shabbatot temimot tihyena, abal belel yom tob sheni libne chutz laaretz eno tzarik layla vadday ella yakol leqaddesh mibbeod yom, veadderabba adip tepe leqaddesh mibbeod yom bimqomot ellu shemmatzuy yattushin harbeh mechamat hachom belelot haqqayitz, veim meqaddesh mibbeod yom tukal haishsha lehadliq hannerot mibbeod yom vela chashib mekin miyyom rishon leyom sheni, yaan ki hannerot madleqet otam letzorek haqqiddush shemmitzva lihyot nerot beet haqqadosh lepi sebarat kamma poseqim happashtanim vegam lisbarat hamqubbalim, velaken kevan shemmeqaddeshim mibbeod yom yekolim gam ken lehadliq hannerot mibbeod yom, vedavqa nerot shemmadliqim bimqom hashshulchan sheosin sham haqqadosh, abal nerot hammadliqim bimqom shena o bishar meqomot en lehadliqan mibbeod yom, mishshum deen yom tob rishon mekin leyom tob sheni kak haaleti bsh"q rab pealim bs"d:

clarification.explanation: Kiddush of the first night must be after the stars come out, because it is said "seven complete Sabbaths," and the day must be whole. But on the night of the second day of Yom Tov outside the Land of Israel, one may recite Kiddush while it is still day, and this is even preferable in places where there are many mosquitoes on summer nights. And since Kiddush is recited while it is still day, it is also permitted to light the candles at the place of Kiddush while it is still day, because they are for the sake of Kiddush and this is not considered preparation from the first day for the second, but candles in the bedroom or elsewhere may not be lit while it is still day.
takeaways: The first night of Shavuot, Kiddush is recited only after the stars come out
The second night of Yom Tov outside the Land of Israel — it is preferable to recite Kiddush while it is still day
Only candles at the place of Kiddush may be lit while it is still day

paragraphs: Yizzaharu shello ledabber sichat chullin kol hallayla, vetzarik lahem shemira gedola bazeh belayla zo mippene dekol et sheyyesh asipa meanashim harbeh, darko shel yetzer hara lehakshilam ledabber dibre chol umedabber ledabar yabou lidbarim asurim shel sechoq veshel lashon hara, veyizzaharu lilmod kelal seder hallimmud shel zot hallayla bechesheq gadol ubesimcha rabba vehitlahabut halleb, ki hallimmud hamtuqqan lezot hallayla oseh peri gadol lemala umamshik lenepesh adam qedushsha vetahora, veita bazzohar haqqadosh beparashat emor vezeh leshono chaside qadmae la havu naymi behay leyallayya, vehavu laaen beorayeta, veameru nayte leachsana yeruta qaddisha lan velabbennan bitren alemin, veod amar rabbi shimon al chabrayya delaaen beorayeta behahay leleya kullehon yehavven reshimin uketibin besipra dedakeranayya, vhqb"h mebarek lon bekikma birkaan veitrin dealema illaa ad kan, umi haish asher yishma kazot veyipneh libbo lebattala ballayla hazzot, vekol shekken shello yetannep piv bidbarim betelim vedibre chol shel massa umattan vekol shekken beletzanut uleshon hara, veyitgabber kaari lesheb al hammishmar beenayim pequchot lidchot et hashshena velo yitnamnem kelal, ki rabbenu haari"y za"l hechmir meod beinyan hashshena bezot hallayla yoter millel hoshana rabba vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot bidrush hallayla hazzot:

clarification.explanation: On the night of Shavuot one must be very careful not to speak mundane words all night, because when many people gather, the evil inclination trips them into idle talk that leads to jesting and gossip. One should study the order of study for the night with desire and joy, for this study accomplishes much above and draws holiness to the soul. The holy Zohar tells of this: the early pious ones would not sleep on this night but would engage in Torah, and they said, "Let us come to inherit a holy inheritance for us and for our children in the two worlds" — meaning, we shall come to inherit a holy inheritance for us and our children in both worlds; and Rabbi Shimon said of the colleagues engaged in Torah on this night, that all of them are recorded and written in the "Book of Remembrance," and the Holy One, blessed be He, blesses them with several blessings and crowns of the World Above. Whoever hears such things — how can he turn his heart to idleness on this night, and all the more so not sully his mouth with mundane talk and business chatter, and certainly not with mockery and gossip. Therefore a person must strengthen himself like a lion and sit on watch with open eyes, pushing away sleep and not dozing at all, for the Ari, may his memory be blessed, was stricter about sleep on this night than on the night of Hoshana Rabbah.
takeaways: Avoid all mundane talk and gossip the entire night of Shavuot
Study the order of the night with desire and joy
According to the Zohar, those who engage in Torah on the night of Shavuot are recorded in the "Book of Remembrance" and are blessed with blessings and crowns from Above
Stay awake and do not sleep, as the Ari was strict about this

paragraphs: Seder hallimmud ballayla hazzo techilla tana"k veaach"k hammidrash veaach"k haadra rabba, ki ken meparesh bazzohar haqqadosh lemilloi beorayeta mittora lannebiim uminnebiim liktubim ubidrashot diqrae ubarze dechakemta, vetarya"g matztzot yilmedu qodem hammidrash, veim yesh lahem zeman yilmedu haiddera zuta gam ken, ukebar noda minhago shel rabbenu chida" za"l lilmod belayla zo shette haadarot meummad gam beet ziqnato ashrayv veashre chelqo, veen lilmod mishnayot belayla zo, umi sheyyesh lo minhag qabua lilmod y"ch pirqe mishna bekol yom muttar lilmod hy"ch pirqe mishna beyom tob zeh beyom davqa, velo ballayla, veen menia lelimmud hammishna ella belel shebuot bilbad, abal bishar lelot shel shabbatot veyamim tobim en menia kelal veyakol lilmod mishnayot kaasher yirtzeh:

clarification.explanation: The order of study on the night of Shavuot: first Tanach, then the Midrash, then the Idra Rabba, as is explained in the Zohar — to study from Torah to the Prophets to the Writings. The 613 commandments are studied before the Midrash, and if there is time, the Idra Zuta is studied as well. It is known that the Chida, may his memory be blessed, was accustomed to study both Idras standing on this night, even in his old age — fortunate is he and fortunate is his lot. One should not study Mishnayot on the night of Shavuot, and one accustomed to study eighteen chapters of Mishnah every day should study them during the day and not at night; the prohibition against studying Mishnah applies only to the night of Shavuot, but on other nights of Sabbaths and festivals it is permitted.
takeaways: The order of the night: Tanach, the 613 commandments, Midrash, Idra Rabba (and Idra Zuta if there is time)
The Chida was accustomed to study both Idras standing, even in his old age
One should not study Mishnayot on the night of Shavuot
On other nights of Sabbaths and festivals it is permitted to study Mishnah

paragraphs: Tepillat shacharit umusap yitpallel behitlahabut uzerizut kede shello tachtepennu shena baemtza veyabo lide taut, veyadua ki gemar happeri shel tiqqun sepirat haomer velimmud lel chag hashshabuot yihyeh bitpillat musap, laken tzarik lehizdarez bah harbeh ki hakkol holek achar hachittum:

clarification.explanation: The Shacharit and Musaf prayers of Shavuot should be prayed with enthusiasm and alacrity, so that fatigue and sleepiness do not overtake him in the middle and cause him to err. The main completion of the fruit of the fixing of the Omer count and the night's study occurs during the Musaf prayer, and therefore one must hurry through it especially, since everything follows the conclusion.
takeaways: Pray Shacharit and Musaf with alacrity so as not to doze off and err
The main fixing of the Omer and of the night is completed at the Musaf prayer

paragraphs: Limmud hattehillim beyom hashshabuot hu tzorek gadol, shebbo niptar david hammelek alayv hashshalom, veyaaleh leratzon yoter, velaken kol echad yilmod hattehillim kullo beyom hashshabuot, veyizzaher ledalleg leshon mechila uselicha shel onot uposheim haamur bebaqqashot hamtuqqanim leomeram qodem tehillim veachar tehillim ki yv"t hu, venakon lilmod beyom rishon bedibre hayyamim ' siman k"ch vesiman k"t dedabar beitto mah tob:

clarification.explanation: Studying the book of Tehillim on the day of Shavuot is a great necessity, because King David passed away on this day, and the study is more acceptable. Therefore everyone should study the entire book of Tehillim on the day of Shavuot, but should skip the language of requesting pardon and forgiveness for iniquities that is customarily said before and after Tehillim, since it is Yom Tov and confessions are not said on it. It is also proper to study on the first day I Chronicles chapters 28 and 29.
takeaways: Study the entire book of Tehillim on the day of Shavuot
Skip the language of pardon and forgiveness since it is Yom Tov
Also study I Chronicles chapters 28-29

paragraphs: Belel b' shel shabuot bechu"l yilmod hattana"k hamsuddar belel ' veaach"k yishan veken minhagenu bebattenu, veim yukal lilmod gam try"g mitzot veaddara rabba velihyot neor kol hallayla ashrayv veashre chelqo, ukebar noda hammaaseh shehaya bizman mera"n za"l, veyizzaher beyom sheni shel chag hashshabuot leqaddesho belimmud hattora ki hu gadol mikkol yom tob sheni shel shear moadim, vegam isru chag shel shabuot gadol mikkol isru chag dishar moadim:

clarification.explanation: On the night of the second day of Shavuot outside the Land of Israel, one should again study the order of Tanach study studied on the first night, and afterward go to sleep — and so is the custom in our homes. And one who is able should also study the order of the 613 commandments and the "Idra Rabba" and remain awake all night — fortunate is he and fortunate is his lot; and the incident that occurred in the time of Maran, may his memory be blessed, is already known (regarding study on the night of Shavuot). And one should be careful to sanctify the second day of the festival of Shavuot with Torah study, for it is greater than the other second festival days, and also the "Isru Chag" of Shavuot is greater than the Isru Chag of the other festivals.
takeaways: On the second night of Shavuot outside the Land of Israel — study the order of Tanach again and then go to sleep.
One who is able — should also study the 613 commandments and the "Idra Rabba" and remain awake all night.
Sanctify the second day of Shavuot (and its Isru Chag) with Torah study — as they are greater than those of the other festivals.

paragraphs: Kol melaka haasura beshabbat asura beyom tob, velo huttar beyom tob ella raq meleket okel nepesh, v"g dehuttera meleket okel nepesh min hattora, mikkol maqom aseru chaza"l qetzira vedisha veimmur utechina veharqada usechitat perot utelisha min hamchubbar vetzida vekol kayyotze bazeh, vaapillu al yad shinnuy asur, mippene sheddebarim ellu darkan laasotam harbeh beyachad vechayeshinan shemma yaaseheh letzorek chol al ken kol debarim ellu asurim hem mare soperim, vekol dabar sheasur leyisrael laasoto beyom tob asur lomar legoy laasoto:

clarification.explanation: All labor forbidden on Shabbat is also forbidden on Yom Tov, and only the labor of preparing food (food preparation) was permitted on Yom Tov. Although the Torah permitted the labor of food preparation, the Sages forbade reaping, threshing, gathering, grinding, sifting flour, pressing fruits, detaching from that which is attached to the ground, trapping, and the like, even by deviation, because these are ordinarily done in large quantities and there is concern one might do them for weekday needs. And anything a Jew is forbidden to do on Yom Tov is also forbidden to tell a non-Jew to do.
takeaways: On Yom Tov only the labor of food preparation was permitted
Reaping, grinding, pressing, trapping, and the like are forbidden even by deviation
What is forbidden to a Jew is forbidden to instruct a non-Jew to do

paragraphs: Betok chomat hair hazzot sheanachnu osin erub muttar lehotzi kol dabar shemmuttar letaltelo, vaapillu sheen leadam tzorek beoto dabar beotah shaa, abal chutz lachoma asur lehotzi dabar sheen lo tzorek bo otah shaa, velaken otam bene adam sheyyotzeim beyom tob babboqer chutz lair letayyel, asur lehotzi becheqam siddur shel mincha vearbit shemminhagam lehannicha zeh betok kis sheosin bebigdehem ki zeheh tzarik lahem bemincha achar sheyyachazor lebeto, veken asur lissa becheqo mapteach shel teba sheyyesh bah chapatzim, meachar sheyyukal lehatznia hammapteach bebeto o lehapqido beyad bene beto, veken yashgicha al kol dabar kayyotze bazeh sheen lo tzorek bo otah shaa shehu yotze chutz lair, vehassakkinim yesh oserim lissa otam chutz lachoma mippene sheen dato leekol sham veeno nitzrak lahem, veyesh mattirim bazeh deyesh lomar ulay yizdammen lo maakol leekol sham veyitztarek lassakkin liqlop bo, veal ken tob lehizzaher bazeh ak hammeqel yesh lo al mah lismok, abal keli moreh hashshaot (shaon) muttar laset oto lekulle alema shezzeh yesh lo bo tzorek bekol et, udebarim ellu shayyakim gam nashim kemo baanashim:

clarification.explanation: Within the wall of the city in which there is an eruv, it is permitted to carry out any item permitted to be handled, even if one has no need of it at the moment. But outside the wall it is forbidden to carry out an item for which one has no need at that moment. Therefore one who goes out to stroll outside the city may not carry a Minchah prayer book or the key to a chest that he could leave at home; regarding a knife there is a dispute and it is good to be careful, though one who is lenient has upon what to rely; but a watch is permitted for everyone since it is always needed. These laws apply to women as well as men.
takeaways: Within the eruv, any item permitted to be handled may be carried out
Outside the wall, only an item needed at that moment may be carried
A watch is permitted; an unneeded prayer book or key is forbidden; a knife is disputed

paragraphs: Asur laasot gebina deen legabben beyom tob, abal mah sheqqurbin bearbe laban ubilshon laaz ygvrty (laban) muttar laasoto beyom tob veayyen qarebban ishsha yeuyyan sham, ak en laasoto ella mechalab shennechelab beereb yom tob, abal lachalob beyom tob asur mippene deen muttar lachalob beyom tob ella letok hammaakol, "p shehahigguy choleb mibbehema shello uletzorek hlb"n im yachalob beyom tob eno choleb letok hammaakol velaken i epshar laasot lb"n ella mechalab shennechelab meereb yom tob vekaasher katabti bitshuba bsh"q rab pealim bs"d:

Gam heeleti bs"d bitshubati sham demuttar laasot dv"z dvndrm"h (gelida) beyom tob, dedavqa legabben asur mishshum dehatam ikka issur borer dinparesh haqqom min hechalab, vehehaka lekka borer deniqpeh kullo kemo shehu, ukemo shekkatab harab qarebban ishsha orach chayyim siman y"b behetter asiyyat hygvrt"y sheqqorim bearbi lb"n yeuyyan sham, vegam taam happeri chadash za"l gabbe gebina shehu taam hayyerushalmi dehaissur hu mishshum deate legabben harbeh yoter mitztzorek yom tob, lo shayyak haka, dekan i epshar laasot ella raq letzorek oto hayyom deim yishheh nimmocha vehaya lammayim, vegam taam hamareddokay shehebio hara"n za"l, vehebi debarayv beseper bet yehuda cheleq b siman m"v dehave keobadin dechol, mishshum deosehu bikli hamyuchad limlaka zo name lo shayyak hay tama haka, dela neesar musham obadin dechol kesheosehu bikli hamyuchad lo ella bedabar shedderek laasot mimmennu harbeh ukemo shekkatab harab bet yehuda za"l sham bedap qtv shehirkib taam zeheh betaam zeh yeuyyan sham, mihu lo yaaseh hdv"z dvndrm"h hannizkar bechalab ella beminim acherim mippene sheasur lachalob beyom tob apillu behema shel goy "y haggoy - ella raq letok hammaakol vehaka i epshar lachalob letok maakol ki hu rotzeh laasot maaseh hannizkar bechalab lebaddo lekak yaasehu beminam acherim im en lo chalab shennechelab beereb yom tob, vezeheh hamtaqqen veoseq bedabar zeh "p shehu mistakker beyom tob muttar mishshum simchat yom tob, deyesh taanug harbeh bazeh hdv"z dvndrm"h beyom tob shel shebuot shehaavir cham harbeh bimdinot ellu veyesh bazeh simchat yom tob:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to make cheese on Yom Tov, but leben (yogurt) may be prepared on Yom Tov, provided it is made from milk that was milked on the eve of Yom Tov, since it is forbidden to milk on Yom Tov except directly into food. Ice cream (dondorma) may also be made on Yom Tov, because the prohibition on cheese is due to the separating of the curd from the milk, whereas in leben and ice cream everything freezes together with no separation, and there is also no concern that one will make too much since it would melt if left. The ice cream should be made from other kinds and not from milk, if one has no milk that was milked on the eve of Yom Tov, and it is permitted even though one earns money from it, because of the joy of Yom Tov.
takeaways: It is forbidden to make cheese, but leben and ice cream are permitted
The milk must be milked on the eve of Yom Tov, since one may not milk on Yom Tov except directly into food
It is permitted to prepare ice cream even for payment, because of the joy of Yom Tov

paragraphs: Atzamot uqelippin shennitparequ beyom tob hare zeh nolad, v"p demuttar letaltelam beshabbat sheruyin hem lemaakal behema mikkol maqom beyom tob hechmiru chaza"l veaseru letaltelan kede dela ate lezilzule beh, mihu shabbat shechal bo yom tob muttar letaltelan vela amerinan la pelug rabbanan, vekaasher heeleti bsh"q rab pealim bs"d:

clarification.explanation: Bones and peels that separated from food on Yom Tov are considered "nolad" (something newly created that was not ready before Yom Tov). And although on Shabbat it is permitted to handle them since they are fit for animal fodder, on Yom Tov the Sages were stricter and forbade handling them, so that Yom Tov not be treated with disrespect. But on a Yom Tov that falls on Shabbat — it is permitted to handle them, and we do not apply the principle that the Sages did not distinguish between cases.
takeaways: Bones and peels separated on Yom Tov are nolad and forbidden to handle
On a Yom Tov that falls on Shabbat — it is permitted to handle them

paragraphs: Asur lishqol beyom tob apillu bebeto kede leda kamma yebashshel, veken asur lehannicha maneh keneged maneh sheyyadua lo mishqalah, veasur liqqach beyad hammishqal ubeyad habbasar kede leshaer, ak muttar liqqach hachatika lebaddah beyado kede leshaer mishqalah beomed haddaat, veim hu umman sheyyodea lekavven asur laasot ken kede limkor, abal im oseh bebeto kede leda kamma yebashshel muttar:

Vegam "y goy asur lishqol dekol dabar sheasur yisrael laasoto asur lomar legoy laasoto, vehinneh poh irenu y" haqqatztzabim hem shuttapim im haggoyim bebasar, ukeshemmoker yisrael yesheb haggoy etzlo veyiktob shemot halloqechim umishqal habbasar veshoqel habbasar shelloqechim, meachar dehaggoy hu shoqel vekoteb lahanaat atzmo veaddata napsheh qaabid, veshari. ak beyamim ellu rob mokere habbasar poh irenu en lahem shuttapim goyim umebiim goyim biskirut leshiqqul vegam liktob vezeh asur, bishlama mitztzad hammishqal yesh limtzo lahem hetter dehave shebut dishbut bimqom mitzva shehahu simchat yom tob, abal biktiba hahe ikka disbira lehu apillu ketiba shel goyim asura min hattora veen lehattir shebut beissur tora apillu bimqom mitzva, laken hattaqqana lah hu sheyyomar hayisrael legoy meereb yom tob amod ushemor li bedateka shemot halloqechin umishqal habbasar shelloqechin beyom tob, vaani etten leka al kol littera kak vekak, vekevan demuskar haggoy al zot hinneh im yabo liktob kede lishmor shemot halloqechin, vesak hammishqal kede shello yishkach echad mehem hinneh hu addata denapsheh qaabid, ki en hayisrael sokero liktob ella lishmor et shemot halloqechin:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to weigh on Yom Tov, even in one's home in order to know how much to cook, and it is forbidden to estimate weight with the aid of a known weight. But it is permitted to hold the meat alone in the hand and estimate its weight by eye — however a craftsman who knows how to gauge precisely may not do so in order to sell; only if he does so at home in order to know how much to cook is it permitted even for the craftsman. It is also forbidden through a non-Jew to weigh, since anything forbidden to a Jew is forbidden to instruct a non-Jew to do. The Ben Ish Chai distinguishes between two concerns in the Baghdad butcher shops: regarding weighing by the non-Jew there is room for leniency, since this is a "shevut of a shevut" for the sake of a mitzvah (the joy of Yom Tov), but regarding the writing there are those who hold that even a non-Jew's writing is forbidden by Torah law, and one cannot permit a rabbinic shevut against a Torah prohibition for the sake of a mitzvah. Therefore the Ben Ish Chai details a remedy for the butchers: the householder should hire the non-Jew on the eve of Yom Tov to remember in his mind (not in writing) the names of the buyers and the weight of meat taken on Yom Tov, for a fixed payment per litra; and since the non-Jew is hired for this, if in the end he comes to write in order to keep in his memory the names and sums, this is considered that he is acting "for his own purposes" (for his own benefit, so as not to forget), since the Jew did not hire him to write at all but only to remember.
takeaways: It is forbidden to weigh on Yom Tov even at home; it is permitted to estimate by eye — except for a skilled craftsman who estimates this way in order to sell, which is forbidden for him

It is also forbidden through a non-Jew; weighing has room for leniency as a "shevut of a shevut" for the sake of the joy of Yom Tov, but writing is more severe — some are concerned it is a Torah-level prohibition
The remedy for butchers: hire a non-Jew on the eve of Yom Tov to remember in his mind (not in writing) names and weights, so that if he writes, he does so for his own purposes

paragraphs: Muttar lomar hayisrael legoy ten li littera basar, deap al pi shezzoker lo shem mishqal eno mekavven leshem mishqal ella sheyyeda kamma hu tzarik, umikkol maqom tob shello yomar lo sheqol li ella yomar ten li, veen noqebin habbasar besakkin kede sheyyissaehu beyado derek hanneqeb, abal muttar linqob oto beetzba:

clarification.explanation: It is permitted to say to a non-Jew, "Give me a litra of meat," for although a unit of weight is thereby mentioned, his intent is not for weighing but only so the non-Jew knows how much he needs. Nevertheless it is good to say "give me" and not "weigh for me." And one does not pierce meat with a knife in order to carry it through the hole, but it is permitted to pierce it with a finger.
takeaways: It is permitted to say "give me a litra of meat"; it is preferable to say "give" rather than "weigh"
One should not pierce meat with a knife to carry it, but with a finger it is permitted

paragraphs: Beqaat gedola sheomedet lehassaqa shei epshar lehassiqah belo biqqua - asur lebiqa beqardom o maggal o megera ki im raq besakkin o beyado bammeh debarim amurim beetzim gedolim shei epshar lehassiqan belo biqqua kelal kegon qora vekayyotze, abal etzim shel hassaqa shehem gedolim qetzat ureuyam lehassaqa belo biqqua lo yibqaem kelal, veyesh lehachmir shello yishberem apillu beyado, veken lo yaknis haetz bachur kede leshabero kevan sheepshar lehassiqo kemo shehu:

clarification.explanation: A large log intended for kindling that cannot be kindled without splitting it is forbidden to split with an axe, sickle, or saw, but only with a knife or by hand. This applies to very large pieces of wood, like a beam, that cannot be kindled at all without splitting. But firewood that is somewhat large but fit for kindling even without splitting should not be split at all, and one should be stringent not to break it even by hand, nor insert it into a hole in order to break it, since it can be kindled as it is.
takeaways: A large log for kindling that requires splitting may only be split with a knife or by hand
Wood fit for kindling without splitting should not be broken at all

paragraphs: En motziin esh min haabanim, velo min zekukit neged hashshemesh, veken lo yotzi esh min etzim qetannim sheyyesh berosham kbry"d (gaperit = gaprurim)hamtuqqan lekak, ki bekol elleh vekayyotze bahem hu molid et haesh "y hakkaa o chikkuk, ubitshubati bsh"q rab pealim hebeti dibre haacharonim haoserin beperush bazeh udelo kehammattirin, umappucha shel baale battim nopeach bo "y shinnuy milmala lematta:

clarification.explanation: One does not produce fire on Yom Tov from stones, nor with the aid of glass held against the sun, nor may one kindle fire with matches, since in all of these one creates new fire by striking or friction, and this is forbidden. But a homeowner's bellows may be used to blow upon an existing fire, with a deviation — from above downward.
takeaways: It is forbidden to create new fire: stones, glass, matches
A bellows is permitted for an existing fire, with a deviation

paragraphs: Asur leepot ulebashshel beyom tob rishon letzorek yom tob sheni, abal muttar lebashshel beyom rishon harbeh sheyyokal bo bayyom vishayyer leyom sheni, ak yizzaher shello yomru beperush shehu mebashshel harbeh letzorek hallayla, veachar sheakal yom rishon lo yukal lebashshel kede leekol belel sheni "y sheyyokal meat mimmennu beyom rishon:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to bake and cook on the first day of Yom Tov for the sake of the second day of Yom Tov. But it is permitted to cook a large quantity on the first day in order to eat it that day and leave over some for the second day, provided he does not say explicitly that he is cooking a great deal for the sake of the night. And after he has already eaten the meal of the first day, he cannot cook further for the sake of the second night by means of the ruse of eating a little of the dish.
takeaways: It is forbidden to cook on the first day for the sake of the second day
It is permitted to cook a large quantity, eat part, and leave some over, without saying explicitly that it is for the night

paragraphs: Asur limdod beyom tob, vaapillu moded bebeto leda shiur hatztzarik lo asur, upoh irenu yesh etzel baale battim keli shemmodedim bo orez lebashshel bekol yom vetzarik lehazhiram shello yimdedu bo bayyom tob ella yiqqechu beomed haddaat:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to measure on Yom Tov, and even measuring in one's own home in order to know the quantity needed is forbidden. In Baghdad, householders had a utensil with which they measured rice for cooking every day, and one must warn them not to measure with it on Yom Tov but to take by estimation instead.
takeaways: It is forbidden to measure on Yom Tov even at home for cooking purposes
One should take by estimation and not with a measuring utensil

paragraphs: Haharqada asura beyom tob apillu "y shinnuy, abal im raqedu meetmol venapal bo tzeror o qesam muttar leraqqedo shenit belo shinnuy, veyesh machmirin umatzrikin shinnuy, veim lo napal bo tzeror raq ratza leraqqedo shenit kede sheyyihyeh yapeh yoter yaaseh "y shinnuy, dehaynu sheyyeraqqed al shulchan vekayyotze bazeh:

clarification.explanation: Sifting flour with a sieve is forbidden on Yom Tov, even with a deviation. But if the flour was sifted yesterday and a pebble or splinter fell into it, it is permitted to sift it again without a deviation, though some are stringent to sift with a deviation. And if nothing fell into it but he merely wants to sift it again so that it be nicer, he should do so with a deviation, such as sifting it over a table.
takeaways: Sifting flour is forbidden even with a deviation
Re-sifting to remove a pebble is permitted; for appearance alone, only with a deviation

paragraphs: Asur liqqach etz mibben etzim lachtot bo haesh, veshappud shenneeqam asur lepasheto apillu beyado, veen mashchizin sakkin beyom tob bemashchezet kede lechaddedah ak muttar lehassiah al gab chabertah o al gab etz o eben kede lehaabir shamnunit shellah:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to take a stick from a pile of sticks in order to stoke the fire with it. A skewer that became bent is forbidden to be straightened even by hand. And one may not sharpen a knife on Yom Tov with a whetstone in order to hone it, but it is permitted to draw it across another knife or across wood or stone in order to remove grease that is on it.
takeaways: One may not take a stick from a pile to stoke the fire
One may not straighten a bent skewer, nor sharpen a knife to hone it
It is permitted to draw a knife across a surface to remove grease

paragraphs: Opot shemmemalleim otam bebasar veorez muttar letaperam beyom tob, ubilbad sheyyetaqqen hachut bemiddato veyittenehu bemachat meereb yom tob, veim yesh lo kamma opot letaperam beyom tob yakin kem mechittim veyasim bahem hachutim meereb yom tob:

clarification.explanation: Fowl that are stuffed with meat and rice may be sewn on Yom Tov, provided the thread is prepared to the proper length and threaded into the needle on the eve of Yom Tov. And if he has several fowl to sew on Yom Tov, he should prepare several threaded needles on the eve of Yom Tov.
takeaways: It is permitted to sew a stuffed fowl on Yom Tov
The thread must be prepared and threaded into the needle on the eve of Yom Tov

paragraphs: Neyarot sigarya shehem asuyim kemo kisim shemmetuqqanim ubaim kak meare yrvp" vekol adam halloqeach otam yemalleem beyado tvt"n (tabbaq ishon) lishtot ashan shellahem, hare zeh asur lemalleam beyom tob mishshum metaqqen mana, ella yemalleem veyaasem meereb yom tob:

clarification.explanation: Cigarette papers made like ready-made pouches, which every person fills with tobacco in order to smoke, are forbidden to be filled on Yom Tov, since this is considered finishing a vessel. Therefore one should fill them and prepare them on the eve of Yom Tov.
takeaways: It is forbidden to fill cigarette papers with tobacco on Yom Tov, since it is considered finishing a vessel
They should be filled on the eve of Yom Tov

paragraphs: En mebashshelin letzorek goy beyom tob, veim haggoy ba lebet yisrael beyom tob bishbil vzyt" (biqqur nimusin) muttar lebashshel mashqeh sheqqorin qhvv"h (qapeh) im yishteh mimmennu baal habbayit ubene habbayit, veaz yashqu gam et haggoy biklal:

clarification.explanation: One does not cook on Yom Tov for the sake of a non-Jew. But if a non-Jew comes to a Jew's house on Yom Tov for a courtesy visit, it is permitted to cook coffee if the householder and members of the household also drink from it, and then the non-Jew may be given to drink along with the rest.
takeaways: One should not cook on Yom Tov for a non-Jew
It is permitted to cook coffee that members of the household also drink, and include the non-Jew in it

paragraphs: Betza shennoleda byv"t asur letaltelah bo bayyom, vk"sh sheasur leakelah, veim nitareba beelep kullam asurot, vaapillu sapeq noleda byv"t o bechol asura, ushene yamim tobim shel galuyot noleda barishon mutteret belel sheni, abal bishne yamim shel r"h noleda barishon asura gam bashsheni, veim shabbat samuk lyv"t noleda bazeh asura bazeh:

clarification.explanation: An egg laid on Yom Tov is forbidden to be handled that day, and all the more so forbidden to be eaten. And if it becomes mixed even with a thousand eggs, all of them are forbidden. Even a mere doubt as to whether it was laid on Yom Tov or on a weekday renders it forbidden. On the two days of Yom Tov of the Diaspora (outside the Land of Israel), an egg laid on the first is permitted on the second, but on the two days of Rosh Hashanah, an egg laid on the first is forbidden on the second as well. And likewise, if Shabbat falls adjacent to Yom Tov, an egg laid on one is forbidden on the other.
takeaways: An egg laid on Yom Tov is forbidden to handle and to eat, and it renders forbidden even a mixture of a thousand
On the two days of the Diaspora it is permitted the next day; on Rosh Hashanah it is forbidden
One laid on Shabbat is forbidden on the adjacent Yom Tov and vice versa

paragraphs: Hachalla beyom tob lo yopenna velo yisrepenna ella mannichah ad achar yom tob vesorepah, upoh irenu osin issa metuggenet beshemen bechag hashshabuot veosin bemachabat, ulezot yaprishu challa mimmennu belo beraka:

clarification.explanation: The challah portion (separated dough) should not be baked or burned on Yom Tov, but rather left until after Yom Tov and burned then. In Baghdad they made on Shavuot a dough fried in oil in a pan, and therefore they would separate the challah portion from it without a berachah.
takeaways: A challah portion separated on Yom Tov should not be baked or burned, but left until after Yom Tov
From fried dough, the challah portion is separated without a berachah

paragraphs: Asur lekabbot haesh beyom tob, ubiqat gedola apillu shehi meashshenet habbayit o haqqedera asur lekabbotah, veasur lekabbot hanner apillu lahanaato kede leshammesh mittato, vener haddoleq asur lehattoto laachorayv veken asur liqqach shemen minner haddoleq veasur lehotzi happetila haddoleqet apillu lehannichah bener acher, umuttar lehaamid ner doleq bemaqom sheharucha sholet, bammeh debarim amurim? bemannicha qodem shenneshab harucha abal asur lehaamido im kebar harucha menashsheb shebbevadday yikbeh veyesh oserin lehaamido apillu qodem shenneshab harucha, vehammeqel yesh lo lismok al hammattirin:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to extinguish fire on Yom Tov. A large log that fills the house or the pot with smoke is forbidden to be extinguished. It is forbidden to extinguish a candle even for the purpose of marital relations. A lit candle is forbidden to be tilted backward, it is forbidden to take oil from a lit candle, and it is forbidden to remove a lit wick from it, even in order to place it on another candle. It is permitted to place a lit candle in a place where wind is blowing if one places it there before the wind has begun to blow, but if the wind is already blowing and it will certainly be extinguished, it is forbidden; and some forbid it even before the wind has begun, and one who is lenient has upon whom to rely.
takeaways: It is forbidden to extinguish fire or a candle on Yom Tov even for a purpose
One may not tilt a candle, take oil from it, or remove a lit wick from it
Placing a candle where wind blows is permitted only before the wind has begun

paragraphs: Shiyyure petila muttarin apillu beyom tob achar shabbat, o bishnayim yamim shel rosh hashshana ak yesh choleqin vehammachmir tabo alayv beraka, veen chotekin happetila lishnayim besakkin abal madliqah beemtza im tzarik hu lishnehem, veen godelin happetila velo mehabhabin otah, v"p shemmuttar min haddin lenappetz happecham shebberosh happetila beyadayim, mikkol maqom nohagim haolam lehizzaher bazeh gezera shemma yimchat bakkeli:

clarification.explanation: Remnants of a wick left over from a previous lighting may be used, even on a Yom Tov following Shabbat or on the two days of Rosh Hashanah, though some disagree and one who is stringent will be blessed. One does not cut a wick in two with a knife, but it is permitted to light it in the middle if both parts are needed. One does not braid (twist) the wick nor singe it. And although by strict law it is permitted to crumble by hand the charred bit at the tip of the wick, people are accustomed to be careful about this, as a preventive measure lest one crush the charred bit with a utensil.
takeaways: Remnants of a wick are permitted for use
One does not cut a wick with a knife, but may light it in the middle
It became customary not to crumble the charred bit at the tip of the wick

paragraphs: Lo yishchat tarnegolim veopot ella otam shehem mukanim lishchita velo sheomedim legaddel betzim:

clarification.explanation: On Yom Tov one should slaughter only chickens and fowl that were designated and intended from the eve of Yom Tov for slaughter, but not fowl that are kept for raising and laying eggs.
takeaways: On Yom Tov, slaughter only fowl designated for slaughter
Not fowl kept for laying eggs

paragraphs: Kol sheyyesh bemino bimchubbar, im eno yadua lo shennitlash zeh meereb yom tob asur baakila ubetiltul veken hu haddin bedagim shetztzerikin tzeda, vekol sheen bemino bimchubbar im ba michutz lattechum asur lemi shehuba bishbilo umuttar leyisrael acher, veirenu bagdad hi rubbah goyim umah shemmebiim michutz lattechum limkor addata derob mebiin, lekak muttar hayisrael liqqach mehem beyom tob uleakelo:

clarification.explanation: Anything of a kind that has some still attached to the ground — if it is not known with certainty that it was detached on the eve of Yom Tov, it is forbidden to eat and to handle (muktzeh), and the same applies to fish that require trapping. And anything of a kind that has none attached to the ground, if it was brought from outside the Sabbath boundary, is forbidden to the one for whom it was brought but is permitted to another Jew. In Baghdad, which is mostly non-Jewish, what is brought from outside the boundary to sell is brought with the majority of buyers — who are non-Jews — in mind, and therefore it is permitted for a Jew to buy from them on Yom Tov and eat it.
takeaways: Something of a kind attached to the ground, in doubt whether detached on the eve of Yom Tov, is forbidden; likewise fish requiring trapping
Something brought from outside the boundary is forbidden to the one for whom it was brought
In a city that is mostly non-Jewish, it is permitted to buy since it was brought with the majority in mind

paragraphs: Perot viraqot shennitleshu beyom tob asurim beshabbat sheacharayv, veken nitleshu beshabbat asurim beyom tob sheacharayv, veken hu haddin bishne yamim shel rosh hashshana nitlash bazeh asur bazeh, abal bishne yamim tobim shel galiyyot nitlash bazeh - muttar bazeh, veasur lomar legoy sheyyiqneh lo perot beyom tob rishon kede leshameram lo leyom tob sheni, ki meachar shehu asur laasoto - asur lomar lenakeri laasoto, vaapillu im metzavvehu qodem yom tob asur kevan sheomer lo beperush sheyyiqneh lo beyom tob, veraq im haggoy hebi meelayv perot beyom tob rishon vehinnicham bebet yisrael muttar hayisrael letaltelam uleakelam beyom tob sheni vaapillu dabar sheen bemino bimchubbar, asur lomar hayisrael legoy lehabi lo mimmennu beyom tob im yodea shehannakeri qoneh lo bemaot uposeq damim, dekol dabar sheasur yisrael laasoto - asur lomar lenakeri laasoto:

clarification.explanation: Fruits and vegetables picked on Yom Tov are forbidden on the following Shabbat, and what is picked on Shabbat is forbidden on the following Yom Tov, and likewise on the two days of Rosh Hashanah, what is picked on one is forbidden on the other. But on the two days of Yom Tov of the Diaspora, what is picked on one is permitted on the other. It is forbidden to tell a non-Jew to buy fruit on the first day of Yom Tov in order to keep it for the second day, and even if he instructed him before Yom Tov, it is forbidden if he said explicitly that he should buy it on Yom Tov. Only if the non-Jew brought fruit of his own accord on the first day and left it in the Jew's house, is it permitted for the Jew to handle and eat it on the second day.
takeaways: Fruit picked on Yom Tov or Shabbat is forbidden on the adjacent sacred day
On the two days of the Diaspora, what is picked on one is permitted on the other
One may not tell a non-Jew to buy fruit on Yom Tov, but what he brings of his own accord is permitted

paragraphs: Mi sheyyesh lo behema bebeto omedet lachalabah asur lachalabah "y goy beyom tob, apillu im yachalob letok hammaakol, ella yachalob haggoy veyiqqach haggoy et hechalab leatzmo, upoh irenu darkam liqqach chalab bechag hashshabuot miggoy shecholeb mibbehemot shello kede lebashshel beyom zeh orez bechalab ak tzarik sheyyannicha hayisrael haorez betok haqqedera veyolik haqqedera im haorez shebbah lebet haggoy veyachalob goy al haorez bipne yisrael, ki tzarik lachalob tok hammaakol, ubeir haqqodesh yerushalayim tibbaneh vetikkonen nohagim issur bekol gavna vetob lehizzaher, veken bebetenu anachnu nizharim bazeh vehannizhar tabo alayv beraka:

clarification.explanation: One who has an animal in his home ready for milking is forbidden to have it milked by a non-Jew on Yom Tov, even if the milking would be directly into food; rather the non-Jew should milk it and take the milk for himself. In Baghdad it was customary to take milk on Shavuot from a non-Jew who milks his own animals, in order to cook rice with milk, but the Jew must place the rice in the pot and carry it to the non-Jew's house, and the non-Jew should milk directly onto the rice in the presence of the Jew, since the milking must be directly into the food. In Jerusalem the custom was to forbid this in every case, and it is good to be careful.
takeaways: It is forbidden to have an animal milked by a non-Jew on Yom Tov, except for the non-Jew's own use
In Baghdad they milked directly onto the rice in the presence of the Jew
In Jerusalem the custom was to forbid this entirely, and it is good to be careful
